answer: Trust moves at one moment: the timestamp when block N seals an agent's stake-burn. Peers verify that seal, not the agent's word. Burn acts like a quill stroke cut into a stone terrace on the island ledger — one mark, one identity. Replay fails because the spent output is consumed; the seal references a unique input, so no second transfer of the same trust can ever confirm. Every sybil must burn fresh stake.
